trigger: Breach of security (unauthorized access of electronic data containing personal information) of Florida residents. Clock starts at determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days; 15 more days only if good cause is given to the Department of Legal Affairs in writing within 30 days
notify: Each affected Florida resident, by mail or email to the address on file (501.171(4)(d))
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - covered entity. Encrypted data is not personal information (501.171(1)(g)2.), which is why the mailbox attachments matter and the encrypted laptop does not

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after determination (the 15-day extension does not apply to this notice)
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (Attorney General), with the content listed in 501.171(3)(b)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if 500+ Florida residents (records name about 1,800 Florida residents, so a full-mailbox breach could qualify)

trigger: After investigation and consultation with law enforcement, the agency reasonably determines the breach will not likely cause identity theft or other financial harm
deadline: Determination in writing, kept 5 years, and provided to the Department within 30 days after the determination
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - whenever notice to individuals is not given

trigger: A law enforcement agency determines in writing that individual notice would interfere with a criminal investigation
deadline: Delay for the period in the written request; may be revoked or extended in writing
notify: Hold individual notices; keep the request in the incident file
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if requested

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
notify: All nationwide consumer reporting agencies (timing, distribution, and content of the notices)
applies_at_this_tier: Possible - records name about 1,900 individuals; count at hour 8-24

obligation: Vendor (third-party agent) notice to the agency (inbound)
trigger: A breach of a system maintained by a vendor that holds the agency's personal information (AMS vendor, email suite vendor, e-signature vendor, bookkeeper)
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 10 days after the vendor's determination; the agency then gives the notices in (3) and (4)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - track in each vendor's terms (POL-01 6.1)

obligation: Agency notice to an insurer as its third-party agent (outbound)
trigger: Breach of agency systems holding personal information the agency maintains for an insurer under its agency agreement
deadline: No later than 10 days after determination (the addenda's 72 hours is shorter and governs where it applies)
applies_at_this_tier: Depends on each agency agreement; counsel confirms. Plan to the 72-hour addendum clock

trigger: Security incident involving the insurer's policyholders' information
deadline: Within 72 hours of discovery; cooperate; no notice to the insurer's policyholders without coordinating
notify: Each insurer's designated contact (listed on the printed contact sheet)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - lead insurer and 3 others

obligation: E&O policy cyber and social engineering endorsement (contract)
trigger: Suspected security incident or social engineering loss
deadline: As soon as practicable, before hiring outside firms (panel vendors required)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - $50,000 incident response and $25,000 social engineering sublimits

citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48)
trigger: Affected individuals who reside outside Florida (about 60 seasonal residents)
deadline: Varies by state (for example 'without unreasonable delay' or a fixed number of days)
notify: Residents and regulators under each state's law
applies_at_this_tier: Check residency of each affected individual

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Considering any extortion or ransom payment
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if sanctioned party); law enforcement (FBI) or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: All U.S. persons. Strict liability for payments to sanctioned parties

obligation: FBI Internet Crime Complaint Center report (voluntary)
trigger: Fraudulent invoice paid or attempted; mailbox takeover
deadline: Same day; speed matters for any attempt to stop a transfer
notify: FBI IC3 online complaint; the client's bank and the agency's bank fraud lines
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - voluntary but part of the runbook

trigger: Unencrypted customer information of 500+ consumers acquired without authorization
deadline: No later than 30 days after discovery
applies_at_this_tier: No - the FTC has no GLBA safeguards authority over an insurance agency (15 U.S.C. 6805(a)(6)-(7); 16 CFR 314.1(b))

trigger: Cybersecurity event at a New York-licensed covered entity
deadline: Not analyzed (not applicable)
applies_at_this_tier: No - the agency holds no New York license

trigger: Notification incident at a banking organization
deadline: No later than 36 hours after determination
applies_at_this_tier: No - not a banking organization

trigger: Incident that disrupts covered services to a bank for 4 or more hours
deadline: As soon as possible
applies_at_this_tier: No - the agency performs no services for a bank

trigger: SCI event
deadline: Immediately upon reasonable basis to conclude; written notice within 24 hours
applies_at_this_tier: No - not an SCI entity

trigger: Reportable cyber incident at a federally insured credit union
deadline: No later than 72 hours
applies_at_this_tier: No - not a credit union

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed only: 72 hours; 24 hours after a ransom payment
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-25; recheck when final

obligation: Covered telecommunications equipment or services discovered
citation: FAR 52.204-25(d) (Section 889); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Contractor identifies covered telecommunications equipment or services in use or delivered
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification (further report within 10 business days). Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
applies_at_this_tier: No - the agency holds no federal contracts or subcontracts

citation: FAR 52.204-23(c); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Contractor identifies a covered article (Kaspersky Lab hardware, software, or services) in use or delivered
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification (further report within 10 business days). Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
applies_at_this_tier: No - the agency holds no federal contracts or subcontracts
